content.thinking:
I'm designing a lava golem with a Genshin-inspired aesthetic: cel-shaded basalt plates, glowing molten seams, and ornate gold filigree accents against an orange pyro glow, drawing loosely from Ruin Guard and Pyro Hypostasis vibes but keeping it original.

Planning the scale at roughly 2.6m tall, towering over a human, and sketching a chunky humanoid skeleton with a hips root joint, a spine chain built from catmull points, a big torso, massive arms, short thick legs, and a small embedded head with glowing eyes done as glow parts. I'm being careful about joint and chain naming conventions since I can't test the API live, favoring explicit joints over chains where ambiguity could cause errors.

I'm working out arm placement with shoulders angled slightly outward and down, elbows and wrists defined along a path, ending in huge basalt-block fists with chunky fingers built from short two-joint chains—keeping track of the total joint budget across both hands.

For symmetry I'll mirror left and right limbs by flipping the X coordinate, naming joints with L/R suffixes. For the golem's stylized look, I'm planning limb cores as low-poly hexagonal sweeps with a glowing molten center, then layering on stacked hexagonal basalt plates like rock columns to build the chunky armor aesthetic.

The gaps between those plates naturally reveal the glowing lava core as seams, so I'll keep the molten parts flat-colored with glow rather than textured, using a few warm tones (yellow-orange, orange, red) for visual richness. For the basalt plates themselves, I'm thinking cel-shaded dark purple-grey with a mottled texture to suggest rough stone.

I want gold filigree accents too—bands at the wrists, belt, crown, and shoulder rims, plus a decorative gold emblem decal on the chest plate using a plane with an SVG texture. A glowing pyro glyph on that chest emblem with a gold ring around it would tie the whole design together nicely.

For the plate shapes, I'm thinking of using hexagonal cylinders instead of boxes—mimicking basalt columns for a distinctive, iconic silhouette, especially for the torso construction.

Since I can't actually render or test this, I'm planning the overall proportions carefully: roughly 2.9m tall so it looms over a human figure, with a stylized chunky build—moderate head, broad shoulders, oversized fists—and sketching out the vertical layout starting from the feet at ground level up through the hips.

Now I'm working through the joint placements for the legs (hip, knee, ankle coordinates with thickness radii) and setting up a polyline chain for each leg parented to the hips, then moving into the spine chain starting from the hip joint upward.

Still placing neck and head joints...

I'm sketching the golem's head as a blocky basalt skull with a glowing molten mouth slit and slanted extruded eyes, placing the jaw as a separate joint beneath the head using explicit world coordinates throughout.

Working out the eye extrusion orientation now — figuring out which axis determines outline direction versus thickness so the eyes face forward correctly, and whether mirroring one eye requires flipping the outline winding rather than just negating an axis.

Now I'm defining the color palette: three basalt tones (dark, mid, light) built from mottled cel-shaded textures with different seeds for variation, plus a warm underglow tint for surfaces facing downward.

Adding ash crust and underglow logic...

Now I'm setting up the gold and lava glow colors as flat hex values for the paint system, then starting to plan the body structure part by part—beginning with the torso's molten core and plated chest sections.

For the torso, I'm laying out a dark basalt pelvis block with a gold belt, then building the abdomen around a glowing spine core, surrounding it with a ring of plates that leave visible gaps for the molten glow to show through.

Working out the ring semantics: each plate's facing axis points outward from the circle, so I orient the box geometry with thickness along that outward direction and figure out how the local up/forward axes align with the bone's direction for proper plate tilt.

For placement, I'm deciding to anchor the ring to the spine2 joint since literal position/direction frames get nearest-joint assignment automatically anyway, which keeps things simple and avoids manual bone lookup.

Actually, to reduce risk I'll skip the ring helper entirely and compute the positions manually with trigonometry, placing each part at an angle around the circle with an outward direction and explicit bone reference for reliability.

Writing the slab helper function...

Working out plate orientation math...

Rather than getting lost in details, I should enumerate the full component list and write reusable helper functions, keeping the part count under a thousand. I'm planning the skeleton joints, then legs: a core sweep through the leg chain with tapering radii for a glowing effect, plus hex-column thigh armor arranged around the bone.

For the thigh armor specifically, I'm designing a ring of five hexagonal columns around the thigh axis, with gaps between them to let the inner glow show through, computing perpendicular basis vectors so the columns align properly along the bone direction. Writing column ring helper...

This same helper can work for forearm, upper arm, thigh, shin, and torso—one reusable function for all the hex-cage armor pieces. I'm also planning gold bands using low-poly torus geometry positioned along each limb segment, plus a large basalt knee cap (icosahedron) with a gold ring, and a tapered column ring for the shin leading into a blocky foot.

Now I'm working out the foot shape with three forward hex-column toes, and placing the leg joint hierarchy—hip, knee, and ankle positions on each side—so the foot attaches cleanly to the ankle tip joint with its bottom resting exactly at ground level.

For zigzag crack polylines, I can sweep along the points with a small diamond section, using tight corner fillets so they read as sharp rather than rounded, and I need to pass an explicit bone reference since the path points aren't tied to one automatically. I'm placing these crack lines slightly offset outward from the plate surfaces so they read as glowing seams on top rather than embedded inside.

Actually, better to use a paint-based crack network across plates instead of manual placement, using cell noise to generate flat orange crack lines that read well under shading even without emissive glow, reserving true glowing parts for the main seams only.

There's also a built-in scales/edge-paint function that could outline cells with orange edges, though the blend is too soft for a hard cel look -- I'd want a custom threshold version instead. I'm also thinking about texel density for crack width given the painted surface area is roughly 40 square meters across the whole golem.

Working out crack color thresholds...

Applying crack patterns to only about half the plates to avoid visual clutter, with cracks rendering their own lit color directly rather than going through cel-shading so they stay bright even in shadow. I also want glowing molten seams between plates for structural emphasis. Now moving on to the torso — sketching pelvis as a hex-ish box with rough dimensions before working out the leg plates.

For the waist I'm designing a reusable band/ring primitive built from a lathed rectangular profile swept around an axis, which works better than a torus for gold belts and cage rings since I can control radius, height, and thickness independently; using 8 segments for smoother rounded bands versus 6 for the hexagonal theme elsewhere.

Now I'm sweeping the spine chain to form the torso core, varying the cross-section radius along the path so it narrows at the abdomen and flares toward the chest, then building the chest itself as a wide trapezoidal cage of plates with an elliptical core whose radii shift smoothly from bottom to top.

For the plate work, I'm planning front pec and ab plates plus back and side rock-slab plates, and setting up a helper function to place chunky, beveled box plates onto the body at given positions.

Still mirroring plate outlines...

Now I'm working out the z-depth placement: pec thickness 0.14 centered around z=0.40, which should align with the torso's front chest surface at roughly z=0.4, so the plates partly embed into the core geometry rather than sitting fully on top.

Instead of fitting the glowing emblem into the narrow gap between pecs, I'll place a diamond-shaped gold-rimmed sternum plate at the chest center, then layer the glowing sun-flame emblem plane just in front of that plate's surface.

Working out the abdomen next: stacking three horizontal rock-textured belly plates of decreasing width between the pelvis top and lower chest, giving a layered abs look beneath the sternum piece.

For the back, I'm planning a spiky silhouette instead of matching plates—a row of gold-capped basalt-crystal hex columns rising along the spine for a jagged, dramatic profile.

Now I'm detailing those spikes as tapered cylinders with glowing orange tips angled outward, then shifting to design a ring of hex columns wrapping around the flanks of the chest for added armor texture.

To avoid clashing with the front plates, I'm writing a helper function that places cage columns only within a specified angular range around the spine axis, using a reference vector to define the zero angle and computing perpendicular basis vectors to distribute columns evenly between the start and end angles.

Each column gets a slightly randomized length and radius for natural variation, positioned using the angular basis vectors and oriented along the bone axis, with some per-column variety in rotation and sizing to avoid a too-uniform look.

For the shoulders, I'm thinking big ornate pauldrons: a rock-like dodecahedron base with hex columns rising crown-like from the top and a gold rim torus, drawing on that ornate Genshin armor trim aesthetic -- possibly using a lathe-shell half-dome profile for the pauldron shape.

Now I'm working out the arm skeleton chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist, with fingers parented to the wrist joint, and sketching overall proportions to figure out total character height between the pauldron columns, back spikes, and head.

For the arms, I want them extended outward so the fists sit clearly away from the torso, adjusting wrist position for better separation. I'm planning the cage-column structure around the upper arm and forearm, with a bigger gauntlet cage on the forearm, and starting on the palm block for the fist.

Designing finger geometry...

Adding a small glowing lava sphere at each fingertip. For hand orientation, I'm working out how the palm hangs below the wrist with fingers splayed outward in x and z, positioning the four finger bases evenly across the palm width before they extend downward.

Still defining joints...

Thinking about adding Genshin-style flair: maybe a halo of floating gold-rimmed shards behind the back, like a pyro ring with glowing orange glyphs, to give it that elemental deity motif without breaking the "nothing floats unsupported" rule too badly.

I'll keep it moderate — a gold ring with small hex-bead ornaments and teardrop flame pendants behind the shoulders, plus simple belt tassels (gold beads and red curved tube sweeps, a few per side) to echo the ornate Genshin aesthetic.

Front belt should get hanging rock-plate "tassets" with gold trim, cords, and glyph decals. I'll design three decorative SVGs for the chest emblem, belt buckle, and pauldron faces.

For textures I'm planning a flame-sun emblem in gold and orange with a glow effect, a non-glowing gold filigree swirl border for the plates and shoulders, and glowing orange rune strips for the forearm and thigh plates. These will be placed as front-facing planes aligned to known surfaces, like positioning the chest emblem just in front of the sternum surface to avoid z-fighting, and I want to be careful about picking the correct surfaces to attach them to.

I'm sketching the helmet shape now: a chunky angular head extruded from a front-view outline that's wider at the brow and narrows toward the chin, with bevels for a stylized Genshin-style silhouette.

For the face details I want glowing angled eye-slits, gold-trimmed brow ridge slabs, and a glowing mouth under a jaw split, with the lower jaw built as a separate extruded block positioned below the main head mass.

The jaw hinges open with a lava-lit glow gap between upper and lower jaws, pivoting forward on an x-axis rotation at the joint. I'm sketching out the vertical layout of the skull, placing the brow and eyes around y 2.68, the upper skull spanning roughly 2.50 to 2.84, and the jaw sitting near y 2.36, just above the neck top at 2.4.

Adjusting the proportions: head height is about 0.4m, so skull center sits near y 2.62 with the jaw around 2.3–2.45, overlapping slightly with the chest/pauldron area for a hunched golem silhouette, with the mouth glow positioned at y 2.45. Now I'm defining the symmetrical outline coordinates for the upper skull extrude shape.

Shaping eyes...

Confirming the winding is CCW, positive area, fine either way. Placing the eye at the front face of the skull with a slight protrusion of 0.01, mirroring geometry for the right side by negating x-coordinates. Now working out the angled gold-trimmed brow slab positioned above the eyes...

Still defining brow geometry...

Shifting to the mouth, I'm setting up a row of small hexagonal spikes to represent teeth, with no nose needed since this is a golem.

For the fangs, I'm picturing glowing hot yellow-white cone teeth lining the jaw, with a lava-glow box tucked behind them for depth, plus large curved basalt horns sweeping back from the brow with gold tips, topped by a three-column hex crown and a gold circlet ornament across the forehead.

Working out the gold headpiece next: a forehead gem (glowing hex/octahedron, orange) set into a diamond-shaped gold plate, flanked by hex-column ear-guards wrapped in gold rings. Then I'm shaping the jaw as a tapered extrusion from cheek to narrower chin, with a small gold chin plate and considering glowing hex columns as a beard detail.

I'm sketching a drippy lava "beard" of three small tapered glowing cones hanging under the chin, then building the neck as a glowing core column caged by six hex columns in a ring, checking joint placement between neck and head for correct aim direction. I'm also verifying overall proportions -- pauldron radius versus head width, chest core height versus shoulder position -- to make sure nothing clips or overlaps awkwardly.

Now I'm working on trapezius plates as slanted slab shapes running from neck to shoulder, trying to figure out the right orientation vectors (outward normal, up direction) so the box geometry tilts correctly on each side.

I'm also considering adding a dramatic back feature—maybe a cluster of hex-column "volcanic crown" formations rising behind the shoulders at varying heights, with glowing ember-spouting tips, like a miniature Giant's Causeway on the golem's back.

Thinking about whether to pair this with a halo ring behind the head, and checking that it won't clash geometrically with the columns—might scale back to seven columns to make room. I want this to feel rich and detailed without ballooning the part count too much, aiming for roughly 350 pieces total while keeping triangle counts reasonable.

Checking the palette count stays within limits with the lava colors and hot white. For part painting, I need to confirm paint applies based on where a part stands when built, so varying seed positions could affect which parts get painted since location drives the paint assignment.

The baked texture relies on UV maps, and I'm verifying BoxGeometry, CylinderGeometry, Polyhedron, and TorusGeometry all have usable UVs, so flat-shading with toNonIndexed shouldn't break anything. I'm also estimating total painted surface area against texel density to make sure the texture atlas doesn't balloon out of control, with crack widths factored into that budget.

I'm settling on paintSize 2048 for crisper edges, accepting a 4096 atlas even though it's heavy, since the harness allows packing up to that size. Now I'm thinking through type safety for the helper functions -- using plain number arrays or THREE.Vector3 for points, and making sure I import the right joint/bone types without leaving unused variables that would fail strict TypeScript checks.

Writing builder setup code...

Defining more color constants...

Still writing rock paint logic...

Adding the flame sun emblem SVG...

Still writing emblem flame paths...

Still writing SVG filigree...

I'm placing the rune decals on the pectoral plates where the surface is flat and known, plus mirroring onto the back plates and pauldron outer faces. For the pauldrons themselves, I'm sketching a rock-dome shape using a low-detail icosahedron scaled to look flatter and wider, then adding a gold rim ring around its lower edge.

Working through the geometry, I'm adjusting the band's radius and vertical position so it sits right at the dome's equator rather than floating or clipping into the sphere, landing on a radius that makes it protrude slightly like a proper equatorial gold trim.

I'm also adding hex columns on top of the dome with a gold ring base, plus some glowing cap details, and considering spike-like teeth around the lower edge of the pauldron using small cones. For rigging, I'm deciding whether the pauldron should attach to the chest bone (static, less intersection risk) versus the shoulder joint (follows arm motion but risks clipping during arm flex tests).

Attaching to the chest for stability, I'm setting up the shoulder pivot position and starting the arm bone chain from there, running through upper arm, elbow, and wrist with a tapering radius profile. I'm sizing the upper arm cage rings, spacing them along the limb length, and giving the elbow a rocky icosahedron joint with a gold ring accent.

Writing elbow spike geometry...

Now I'm sizing the forearm gauntlet -- a wider cage with thicker struts, plus gold bands at both ends whose radius needs to clear the cage's outer profile so they sit properly over it.

For hands, I'm planning a hex-ish palm box with a gold wrist cuff, then moving on to define the joint hierarchy starting from the hips as the root.

Hips become the root joint, and the spine chain builds up from there through spine1, spine2, and chest using a catmull curve through three points, with the chest as the tip joint aimed upward along the end tangent. I'm considering whether the core should be a sweep along this spine chain to form a tube shape.

For the core tube, I'm defining the radii to taper slightly as it goes up, but I'm worried round caps would dome too high above the chest tip, so I'll switch to flat caps instead. I'll extend the spine path's top point a bit higher so trapezius plates can properly cover the chest area, with the shoulders and neck joints positioned just above that.

Now I'm working out the front plate positions, calculating how far forward in z the chest and pec pieces should sit at each height so they align with the tapering torso radius, then setting the pec plate's center depth and thickness so it spans the right z-range.

Then I check the sternum hex plate's depth and size against the surrounding pec plates, making sure the emblem plane and hex outline project further forward so they overlap correctly and the pec inner edges tuck behind the hex rather than poking through.

I'm now mapping out the pec plate polygon points, noticing one vertex (0.62) overshoots into the pauldron zone, so I pull it back to 0.58 to keep the plates from overlapping the shoulder armor. Checking the winding order confirms the outline is CCW, and mirroring it for the other side by negating x and reversing the point order keeps that same CCW orientation.

For the gold trim, I'm planning to make a slightly larger gold plate sitting behind the pec plate (lower z, scaled up ~1.08 about its centroid) so its edges peek out beyond the pec outline, creating a visible gold rim border around the pec plate from the front.

I'm sketching a reusable `plate` helper that builds the rock extrusion plus an optional gold trim underlay, with a facing parameter to flip the outline orientation for front- vs back-facing plates.

Now I'm checking the extrude options signature and moving on to a `cage` helper that generates a row of connecting rock segments between two points, parameterized by count, radius, taper, and color.

Still writing cage geometry logic...

Still writing shape placement...

Defining a band helper that lathes a ring profile around a bone axis with given radius, height, and width, needing explicit tuple typing on the outline array so TypeScript doesn't widen it to number[][].

Mapping the mirror function over outline points to negate x while keeping y, then reversing the array—the typing works fine since destructuring a union tuple still exposes indices 0 and 1. I'm also checking that the lathe's outline input type and axis parameter align with the expected types.

For the seam glow rods, I'm defining a helper that sweeps a polyline along a bone with a small polygonal cross-section and lava-colored glow material, confirming that passing a tuple array as points satisfies the polyline function's number array requirement. I'm also verifying that sweeping with a single rigid bone and flat caps produces the expected mesh output from glow().

Now starting to lay out the skeleton joints, beginning with the hips joint as the spine root at a fixed position.

Building out the spine chain from hips through chest using a catmull-rom curve, then adding neck, head, and jaw joints with their parent relationships, positions, and aim targets, checking that joint placement matches the skull and mouth geometry coordinates.

For the jaw's hinge rotation, I'm deciding to pose it slightly open (around 7-8 degrees) after building its child parts so teeth and other elements stay correctly parented and move together with the jaw bone, rather than posing before construction which would misalign world coordinates.

Moving on to legs now.

Writing leg chain setup...

Still writing cage geometry...

Still designing leg armor pieces...

Now I'm working out the foot geometry—sizing the ankle box and adding a greave rock for coverage at the joint, then shaping toe segments as angled hexagonal cylinders positioned forward and down from the foot.

Still writing foot details...

Positioning pelvis relative to the hip joint and abdomen cage, then working out the gold belt as a slightly oversized box plate wrapping around the pelvis rather than a lathe ring, since a round shape wouldn't fit the box geometry well.

Now I'm adding a hexagonal gold buckle with a glowing gem at the front of the belt, then shaping tasset plates that hang below it using a tapered outline. I'm checking that these hang in the gap between the thighs without colliding, since the legs' inner edges nearly meet at the center.

Rechecking the depth math: belt front sits at z=.29, so a tasset front of .46 would float oddly ahead of it, like a loincloth pinned to a lip rather than hanging naturally. I'm repositioning the tasset closer, around z=.34, so it tucks against the belt while still clearing the thigh columns at their front edge.

Settling on a tasset width of .3, centered at z=.36, thickness .06, hanging from y=1.27 down to .82, which clears the thighs fine. For the gold tassels hanging below, I'm placing two cords near x=±.09, using a red cloth rod sweep for the cord and a small gold bead sphere for the tassel head, keeping them in front of the thighs so they don't clip into the legs.

Now moving to the abdomen: I'm laying out three ab slabs around z=.33-.38 at increasing y values, checking they stay narrower than the torso core radius so they read as raised highlights rather than filling the whole surface. I'm also planning hex-column cages along the torso flanks (not front/back) by defining a reference vector and sweeping an angle range that lands on the left side of the body.

I'm sizing the flank cage columns against the core's elliptical radius at those heights to make sure the columns sit flush against the torso surface, then shifting to the back where I'll place two shoulder-blade-shaped rock plates with cracked filigree, positioning them slightly behind the core surface and sketching the outline points for each blade shape.

I need to handle mirroring carefully: since front pec plates use positive-x outlines for the world's left side, back plates need the opposite mirroring convention to stay consistent with that frame, so I'm writing a small helper that picks the correct point set or its mirror depending on side.

Now I'm working out the back spine spikes — seven of them spaced along the y-axis, positioned at varying depths and sizes, with directions that tilt increasingly upward toward the top of the spine.

Still working out spike geometry...

Now I'm placing a halo ring behind the head, positioning it around the neck/head height with its axis oriented so it sits behind the figure.

Adding 8 radiating gold spikes and 4 gem glows at the cardinal points, then working out support struts connecting the halo ring to the back crown plate near the shoulders, computing rod endpoints from ring angles to anchor points on the back.

But I realize the halo radius pushes its top past 3.0, exceeding the intended total height for a ~3m golem — I should shrink the halo to R=0.5 and lower its center slightly so the top sits around 2.85, keeping it under the head and crown height.

Repositioning the halo and crown columns, I'm keeping the ring behind the back plates at z=-.55, while pulling the crown columns forward to z=-.3±.1 so they don't poke through the halo plane. For the seven hex crown columns I'm arranging them in an arc with tapered heights, tallest in the center, to form a crown-like silhouette behind the head.

Now I'm adding glowing hex-capped spikes with lava-colored tips, then building the neck structure—a short glowing core rod plus a five-column cage ring, both assigned to the neck joint/bone. After that I'm sketching out the head and jaw bone groups, and starting to recompute the head's outline geometry from vertical offsets to shape the skull.

Working out skull, jaw, and mouth placement, then placing a glowing interior box to create a lit mouth slit between them before adding downward-pointing cone teeth along the skull's front edge...

Checking tooth tip positions against the skull bottom, the lower teeth tips would slightly penetrate the skull volume, but since the jaw is slightly open it should read fine visually. I'll stagger the teeth positions along x so upper and lower rows interleave naturally rather than overlapping directly.

I'm settling on a flat cream color for the teeth rather than a glowing one, keeping the mouth interior glow separate for contrast. For the chin area, I'm skipping a gold plate and instead adding a few lava drip sweeps beneath the jaw using tapered glow tubes attached to the jaw bone.

Now I'm shaping the horns as curved paths sweeping back from the skull, but reconsidering the height since the first attempt pushed too close to the model's total ~3.2m scale. I'm revising the curve to angle outward and droop downward instead, giving a more ram-like silhouette that stays dramatic without overshooting the proportions.

Thinking through the horn material next, I want hexagonal rock-colored sections with a gold ring near the base and a glowing lava tip. Since glow would apply to the whole mesh if I use one continuous sweep, I'm considering splitting it into two sweeps sharing the same path and options—one rock-colored for most of the length, one glowing near the tip—so only the end portion lights up.

I'm defining a radius function keyed on the source parameter t so the taper stays smooth across both halves, and setting cap styles so the boundary between the two sweeps looks seamless rather than showing round bumps. For the face, I'm planning glowing eyes, brows, a forehead gem, and small horizontal cylinder ears at each side with their own gold accent rings.

Still working out ear glow discs, skull crown columns, and a gold forehead plate with an embedded octahedron gem, aiming to keep proportions consistent with the head's existing geometry.

Now shaping the brow ridges, positioning them as protruding extrusions above the eyes with a near-joined center, and considering a gold trim rod along the lower brow edge.

Adding a zigzag glow seam across the flat skull top, then double-checking the extrusion depth settings for the overall shape.

Now defining the arm chains for each side: shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints with their coordinates and parent-child relationships back to the chest. I'm computing the upper-arm and forearm direction vectors and lengths, then positioning the palm center relative to the wrist.

Positioning the palm box geometry, the gold cuff band at the wrist, and spacing out the finger base points along the z-axis for each hand.

Still laying out finger geometry...

Checking neck and shoulder positioning so the pauldron sits flush against the pec without gaps, then working out the dome and gold equator band dimensions for the pauldron geometry.

Still writing pauldron geometry...

Writing rune glyph SVG...

Then I'll drop the stray circle and set the stroke color to white, skip the back plate runes, and place the emblem as a plane on the chest bone with its own texture plus a glow effect.

I'm positioning a gold filigree plane over the tasset front, sized and centered to align with the tasset's outline, letting the rock show through the transparent gaps since it's unlit flat artwork using its own colors. I'm also planning a gold underlay hex beneath the sternum rim via a trim parameter, and considering adding subtle rib glimpses with a glowing "heart" core on the chest.

For the belly, I want lava glow visible through gaps between the ab slabs, using a banded color function that shifts hotter toward the chest—red near the bottom transitioning to orange then yellow. The legs get a simpler two-band gradient from red to orange, and I'm also sketching out belt tassels as hanging rods plus small floating ember sparks scattered near the upper body for atmosphere.

I'm settling on roughly 10 ember particles positioned in a loose cylinder around the golem's torso height, skipping extra floating rock shards and ground plinth details to avoid bloating the part count, since cracks already cover the "worn" look I wanted.

Totaling up the piece counts per limb and torso/head/halo gets me to around 270 parts, which feels reasonable. I'm now considering adding small gold rivet studs on the plates, which would need a helper function to generate and merge the rivet geometry onto each bone's surface points.

Still placing rivet coordinates...

Checking the rune decal placement relative to the rivets, it fits within the pec plate without overlap, and mirroring only needs to flip x-coordinates since the texture itself doesn't require mirroring. I'll skip extra inked edge outlines and move to writing the final code, watching for TypeScript strictness issues like unused locals.

Writing final code...

Still defining helper types...

Now I'm setting up the build function itself, creating the builder with a name and paint size, initializing a seeded RNG, and confirming rock paints can live at module level since determinism only depends on the RNG seeded inside build.

I'm writing helper functions for picking rocks and creating hexagonal cylinder pieces, working through the cylinder geometry parameters so the tapered top aligns correctly with the bone's direction vector.

Adding glowing ember and gem helpers...

Writing the band helper function with a lathe profile, checking that the outline point type and axis height direction line up correctly.

Now I'm sketching a plate helper that optionally extrudes a trim outline slightly in front, with underlay thickness and bevel, and working through whether scaling the outline needs to account for the centroid offset so it doesn't shift off the origin.

Writing mirror and grow helpers...

Writing the import statements...

Still drawing the flame emblem...

Building the torso's lava-core sweep...

Checking placement of the belt and abdomen slabs relative to the pelvis and chest, I'm spotting potential overlap between the abs' top slab and the inner pec geometry around y 1.66–2.06, which I need to adjust the widths or offsets to avoid.

I'll stack two ab slabs below the sternum with a thin glowing gap before the pecs begin, then split each slab into left/right halves with a glowing center seam to create four distinct plates.

Shifting to the trapezius slabs, I'll use a Box with dir and up vectors to orient it diagonally toward the chest, setting up so the local axes align width along x while leaning toward the up direction.

I'm checking the fit against the neck cage and head width — the trapezius slab sits comfortably under the head and overlaps the pauldron region. But comparing the core's flat top at y=2.14 against the slab's bottom at 2.22, there's a small gap, so I'm adding a chest cap plate to bridge that space and give the trapezius proper support underneath.

Now I'm planning additional details: a gold collar band wrapping the neck base, the neck cage geometry itself, and then the halo assembly — a lathed gold ring with an inner glow ring plus a set of bead ornaments positioned around it.

Still working out positions for the ornamental cones, gems placed at cardinal points on the ring, and connecting struts...

Checking the overall height budget: with the ring radius and crest cones added, total height comes to roughly 3 meters, which feels right, so I'm settling the halo center and crown column placement around that figure.

Now I'm checking for intersections between the halo ring and the spine spikes on the back crown — tracing their z-extents and tilt angles against the ring's plane to confirm they clear each other at the lower edge of the ring's height range.

Shortening to .2 length confirms tip clearance. Now I'm computing the spike base positions along the back plates, placing six spikes evenly from y 1.4 to 2.05 at a rear z of -.36 so they protrude from the back plates without colliding with the ring.

That tip actually hits -.52, conflicting with the ring, so I move the ring to z -.62 and shorten the spike length slightly to keep clearance. I check the halo struts connecting ring to back crown, the crown column angles, and now position the back spikes between the plate gaps near x=0.

I'm adding a central keel plate at the back to tie things together structurally. With spacing resolved, I'm ready to assemble the final code.

Writing build function and skeleton...

Still writing leg chain setup...

Still defining limb cages...

Adjusting the gem embedding position and knee cap scaling for better alignment with the shin front. Now I'm setting up the arm chain with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints, making sure joint names stay unique across limbs for finger naming later.

Adding glow tube and cage geometry...

Comparing the palm width against the forearm radius, the fist looks too small relative to the gauntlet, so I'm enlarging the palm box and repositioning it slightly lower to better match proportions, then adjusting finger spacing and radii to fit the wider base.

Modeling the fingers as segmented chains with varying lengths—shorter outer fingers, longer middle ones—plus a separate thicker thumb chain angled outward from the palm.

For the fingertips I'm adding glowing hex gem caps with flat ends, and giving each finger a sweep profile using flat hex caps for a chunkier look. Finally I'm setting up the elbow as an icosahedron ball joint.

Writing spike helper function...

Now thinking about the head and considering making eyes use a cheaper glow effect.
